reasoning: No performance data yet, so I'm testing new ground. Science, space and animals are covered, but history isn't, so this tries a history and deep-time angle. 'Things that happened at the same time' posts tend to get shared because each slide resets your sense of time and invites debate in the comments. A carousel with cards suits a save-worthy list of 7 short, checkable facts. I'm also trying palette 1, which hasn't been used yet, and an opinion-style question to compare comment rates later.
topic: Surprising timeline overlaps in history and prehistory
hook: Timelines that will break your brain

slides.title: Cleopatra and the Moon
slides.body: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
slides.image_prompt: The Great Pyramid of Giza at dusk with a bright full moon rising above it, golden sand, cinematic lighting

slides.title: Mammoths and pyramids
slides.body: Woolly mammoths survived on Arctic Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago, after the Great Pyramid was built.
slides.image_prompt: A woolly mammoth standing on snowy Arctic tundra under a pale sky, realistic, cold blue light

slides.title: Oxford vs the Aztecs
slides.body: Teaching at Oxford began by 1096. The Aztec city of Tenochtitlan was founded in 1325, over 200 years later.
slides.image_prompt: Old stone university towers and spires in warm morning light, medieval architecture, no people

slides.title: Sharks before trees
slides.body: Sharks have existed for about 450 million years. The first trees appeared around 385 million years ago.
slides.image_prompt: A shark gliding through deep blue water beneath the silhouette of an ancient fern-like forest at the surface
slides.credit: Charles J. Sharp (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

slides.title: T. rex vs Stegosaurus
slides.body: Stegosaurus lived about 150 million years ago, T. rex about 68. T. rex is closer in time to us than to Stegosaurus.
slides.image_prompt: A Stegosaurus skeleton and a T. rex skull displayed in a dim museum hall, dramatic spotlight
slides.credit: Gary Todd from Xinzheng, China (CC0) via wikimedia

slides.title: Fax before the phone
slides.body: Alexander Bain patented an early fax machine in 1843, more than 30 years before Bell's telephone in 1876.
slides.image_prompt: A brass Victorian telegraph-style machine on a wooden desk with coiled wires and paper strips, warm vintage light

slides.title: Nintendo and the Ripper
slides.body: Nintendo was founded in 1889 to make playing cards, just one year after the Jack the Ripper murders in London.
slides.image_prompt: Traditional Japanese hanafuda playing cards scattered on a dark wooden table beside a gas lamp, foggy Victorian mood

caption:
History feels like neat chapters, but the chapters overlap in strange ways. A few woolly mammoths were still alive on a remote Arctic island while Egyptians were stacking pyramid stones.

Swipe through 7 timelines that sound wrong but are completely true.
